reference.name: Himalayas (Garhwal–Kumaon Himalaya as seen on the Brahma Tal route)

sources.quote: is a mountain range in Asia separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
The Himalayas span five countries: Nepal, India, China, Bhutan, and Pakistan.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: The Himalayas; locality/region left empty; India correct for the part seen on this Uttarakhand trek.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Region lists Uttarakhand (where Brahma Tal is) plus Himachal Pradesh; both are Himalayan states, acceptable for the range.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Locality Jaipur (Rajasthan) is hundreds of km from the Himalayas and unrelated to the Brahma Tal route.

sources.quote: continuing tectonic processes that began some 50 million years ago when the Indian and Eurasian continents first met
The impinging of the two landmasses has yet to end.

facts.rationale: USGS: India–Eurasia collision began ~50 Ma (40–50 Ma) and continues.

sources.quote: The Himalayas span five countries: Nepal, India, China, Bhutan, and Pakistan.

facts.rationale: The Himalayas span five countries; Afghanistan is not one (it lies in the Hindu Kush, which borders the Himalayas).

sources.quote: The Himalayas consists of four parallel mountain ranges from south to north: the Sivalik Hills on the south; the Lower Himalayan Range; the Great Himalayas
consists of three sub-ranges: (1) the Higher- or "Tethys" Himalayas, (2) the Lesser Himalayas, and (3) the Siwaliks.

facts.rationale: Sivalik (outer foothills), Lesser/Lower Himalaya, Great Himalaya are the parallel ranges.

sources.quote: continuing tectonic processes that began some 50 million years ago when the Indian and Eurasian continents first met
The Himalayas were uplifted after the collision of the Indian tectonic plate with the Eurasian plate

facts.rationale: A mountain system formed by plate collision over tens of millions of years, not founded by a Portuguese mission in 1742.

sources.quote: is a mountain range in Asia separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.

facts.rationale: Mountain range separating the Indian subcontinent's plains from the Tibetan Plateau, i.e. along its northern edge.

sources.quote: The name of the range hails from the Sanskrit Himālaya (हिमालय 'abode of snow')
from the Sanskrit Himālaya (हिमालय 'abode of snow'), from hima (हिम 'frost/cold') and ālaya (आलय 'dwelling/house')

facts.rationale: Everest 8,849 m (8,848.86) is correct, but no reliable source found for the claim that the Himalayas contain the majority of the world's 7,000 m peaks (Wikipedia gives only 'more than 100 peaks exceeding 7,200 m'; many 7,000 m peaks are in the Karakoram/Pamir/Hindu Kush).

sources.quote: Location on the border between Koshi Province, Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China
Four eight-thousanders can be seen, Makalu (8,462 m), Everest (8,848 m), Cho Oyu (8,201 m), and Lhotse (8,516 m).

facts.rationale: Everest is on the Nepal–China border; several other eight-thousanders are in the range.

sources.quote: The Himalayas span five countries: Nepal, India, China, Bhutan, and Pakistan.

facts.rationale: India, Nepal, Bhutan, China (Tibet) and Pakistan.

sources.quote: The name of the range hails from the Sanskrit Himālaya (हिमालय 'abode of snow')
from hima (हिम 'frost/cold') and ālaya (आलय 'dwelling/house')
The Himalayas consists of four parallel mountain ranges from south to north: the Sivalik Hills on the south; the Lower Himalayan Range; the Great Himalayas
consists of three sub-ranges: (1) the Higher- or "Tethys" Himalayas, (2) the Lesser Himalayas, and (3) the Siwaliks.

facts.rationale: Parallel ranges: Great, Lesser (Lower) and Outer (Sivalik) Himalaya.

sources.quote: The range has some of the highest peaks on Earth, including the highest, Mount Everest.
is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. It lies in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas

facts.rationale: Everest, the highest mountain, is in the Himalayas.

sources.quote: The range has some of the highest peaks on Earth, including the highest, Mount Everest.
The Himalayas span five countries: Nepal, India, China, Bhutan, and Pakistan.

facts.rationale: Contains the highest peaks on Earth; spans India, Nepal, Bhutan, China (Tibet) and Pakistan.

sources.quote: The Himalayas were uplifted after the collision of the Indian tectonic plate with the Eurasian plate
The impinging of the two landmasses has yet to end.

facts.rationale: Formed by the continuing India–Eurasia collision.

sources.quote: continuing tectonic processes that began some 50 million years ago when the Indian and Eurasian continents first met
The impinging of the two landmasses has yet to end.

facts.rationale: USGS: collision began ~50 Ma and continues.

sources.quote: Some of the world's major rivers, the Indus, the Ganges, and the Tsangpo–Brahmaputra, rise in the vicinity of the Himalayas

facts.rationale: Indus, Ganges and Brahmaputra rise in the vicinity of the Himalayas.

sources.quote: The Himalayan range encompasses about 15,000 glaciers
Some of the world's major rivers, the Indus, the Ganges, and the Tsangpo–Brahmaputra, rise in the vicinity of the Himalayas

facts.rationale: About 15,000 glaciers; source region of the Ganges, Indus and Brahmaputra.
